item.title: Water Cycle With Exact Labels

turns.text: Make a 10-second widescreen water-cycle explainer with a friendly voice-over you write. Show water rising, clouds forming, then rain. Label those stages exactly “Evaporation”, “Condensation”, and “Precipitation”, in that order. No other on-screen text.

item.tests: Tests exact rendered labels, correct stage mapping, and coordinated original narration in a short explainer.

answer_sheet.Exact on-screen labels: Evaporation; Condensation; Precipitation. Use that capitalization and order, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Other text: No other on-screen text, including subtitles.
answer_sheet.Voice and language: Friendly English voice; specific voice is your call.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second widescreen video has a friendly, intelligible English voice-over explaining the depicted cycle.
Water rises as vapor, clouds form, and rain falls, in that order.
The visible labels read exactly 'Evaporation', 'Condensation', and 'Precipitation', with no misspellings.
Each label is legible and appears with its corresponding stage, in the requested order.
After the follow-up, the final result is vertical 9:16 (the user changed the shape from widescreen 16:9); everything else is as before.

changed_by.say: actually, make it vertical, for stories, and keep everything else the same.

style.prompt: Create a precisely 10-second widescreen educational water-cycle explainer, with generated spoken English audio. Friendly, clear, colorful 2D motion-graphics animation for general audiences. One coherent landscape with blue water below, warm sunshine, sky above, and simple soft clouds. Locked wide camera; readable clean composition. Three successive stages in exactly this order, each with one large correctly spelled label. 0–3.3 seconds: sunlight warms the water and glowing blue vapor particles and upward arrows rise visibly from its surface. Show ONLY the label "Evaporation" during this stage. 3.3–6.6 seconds: follow the rising vapor as it cools and collects into fluffy clouds; show cloud formation clearly. Replace the first label with ONLY "Condensation". 6.6–10 seconds: clouds release clearly visible rain droplets falling back to the water. Replace the second label with ONLY "Precipitation". Labels must be exactly these words, in this order, high-contrast, large, stable, crisp and centered within safe margins. Never display two stage labels simultaneously. Absolutely no other on-screen text: no title, subtitles, captions, narration text, numbers, credits, logos or decorative writing. Audio: a warm friendly narrator speaks the following exact script smoothly across the full 10 seconds, at a brisk but clear conversational pace: "Sunlight warms water, and it rises as vapor. It cools into clouds, then falls as rain. That's the water cycle!" Align rising water with the first sentence, cloud formation with 'It cools into clouds', and rainfall with 'then falls as rain'. Spoken narration is essential; do not replace it with on-screen captions. Very soft gentle water ambience underneath, no overpowering music. Finish with rain returning to the water.
